rows: Isadora Duncan at the Parthenon

Edward Steichen photographed the dancer Isadora Duncan performing among the columns of the Parthenon in Athens. She is a tiny figure in the huge, shadowy temple. Duncan danced barefoot in flowing robes and helped invent modern dance.
How do the huge columns make the dancer seem?
The Dancing Trees
Tree branches swirl against the sky like dancers in a picture made at Lake George. Alfred Stieglitz loved to find shapes and rhythms in nature.
What shapes do you see in the branches?
Music: A Sequence of Ten Cloud Photographs

Stieglitz photographed clouds because critics said his portraits were successful only because of his famous sitters. He wanted to show that a picture of only sky and clouds could make people feel emotions like music does.
What kind of music would this sky play?
Thomas Edison
Thomas Edison invented the practical electric light bulb, the phonograph and a movie camera, among over a thousand patents. In this portrait he sits calmly, in his seventies.
What would you invent?
First Snow and the Little House
A small house stands in the snow at Lake George, New York. Stieglitz photographed the same estate for years, in all seasons, making simple scenes feel quiet and personal.
What would you do in the first snowfall?
Leonora Hughes
Leonora Hughes was an American dancer who became famous in Paris in the 1920s. Edward Steichen photographed her with a cloche hat and pearls, the style of the time.
What do you notice about the fashion?
Oklahoma Madonna
A mother sits near a window holding her baby, in a plain room. Lewis Hine photographed families in need for relief organizations, so people would see who they were helping.
What would you give this family?
The Park at Sceaux
Eugène Atget photographed a misty park near Paris in early spring. The bare trees and dim light make it feel like a quiet dream.
What time of day do you think it is?
A Girl in Swedish Folk Costume
A young girl wears a white cap and a bright red, yellow and blue costume with braids. This early color photograph preserves the vivid colors of Swedish folk dress.
Which colors in the costume stand out the most?
The Czechoslovak Delegation at Locarno

In 1925 leaders from several European countries met in Locarno, Switzerland, to agree on treaties to keep peace after the First World War. This color Autochrome shows the delegation from Czechoslovakia.
Why do you think countries have such meetings?
The Polish Pavilion, Paris
In 1925 Paris held a huge fair of modern design, the exhibition that gave the Art Deco style its name. The Polish pavilion shows the clean lines and decoration that fair made famous.
What shapes do you notice in the pavilion?
Maurice and Barbara Bennett
Two dance partners pose close together in a dramatic embrace. Edward Steichen photographed celebrities for Vanity Fair and Vogue, and made dance look romantic and daring.
What dance do you think they are performing?
Still Life with Lemons and a Siphon
Emmanuel Sougez photographed lemons, a blue soda siphon and printed paper on a table. In the 1920s, photographers began to see ordinary objects as pure shapes and colors.
What shapes can you find in the arrangement?
Coiffeur, Palais Royal
Eugène Atget photographed a hairdresser's window in Paris full of mannequin heads in wigs. The Surrealist artists loved this picture because it looks strange and dreamlike.
Why does a window full of heads feel odd?
From Room 3003, The Shelton
Alfred Stieglitz and Georgia O'Keeffe lived high in the Shelton Hotel in New York. From their window, Stieglitz photographed the growing skyscrapers and factory chimneys beyond.
What would it be like to look out over the city from so high?
Emperor Bao Dai
Bảo Đại became the emperor of Annam, in what is now Vietnam, as a boy. This color portrait shows him in a dark outfit and cap, as a teenager preparing to rule.
What would it be like to be an emperor as a teenager?
Paul von Hindenburg
Paul von Hindenburg was a German general and then president of Germany. This color autochrome from a German magazine shows him in a dark suit with a medal.
What do you notice about his face and moustache?
Two Kurdish Men
Albert Kahn's photographers took color pictures of people all over the world. These two men from the Bahdinan Kurds, in colorful clothes, were photographed on glass plates.
Which parts of their clothing do you find most colorful?
Edwina St. Clair
Edward Steichen became chief photographer for Vogue and Vanity Fair in the 1920s. He photographed this actress in the sleek Art Deco style.
How would you pose to look glamorous?
Boardwalk
Walker Evans was a young photographer in 1929, finding beauty in plain things around him. In this early picture, a woman walks on a boardwalk in a summer dress.
What season does it feel like?
From My Window at An American Place, North
Stieglitz photographed the New York skyline from the window of his gallery. Tall buildings crowd the sky in a hazy gray, as New York grew upward.
How many skyscrapers can you count?
Atop the Empire State Building
Lewis Hine climbed the Empire State Building as it was built to photograph workers high above New York. Here a man works on the mast with a flag as the city spreads out below.
Would you be brave enough to work up there?
Georgia O'Keeffe: Hands and Horse Skull
Alfred Stieglitz photographed O'Keeffe's hands as she held a horse skull she had brought back from New Mexico. She painted bones and skulls of the desert as symbols of beauty.
Why would a painter love a bone?
